span.p:
SC-004 exception, should
Given A freight operations manager reads the grade of section 7. A finding says that a requirement names a component, "consignment".

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: When They refute the finding: "consignment" is their domain's word for one shipment, not a part of the product.

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They see the finding checked against the document

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They see that the glossary defines "consignment" as a domain term

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They see the finding dropped, and a line telling them it was dropped

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p: They see the grade without that finding

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: Then The refuted finding, which the document does not support, is not in the report, the expert sees that it was dropped, and the grade no longer counts it.
